questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two resistors of resistance, $100\,\Omega$ and $200\,\Omega$ are connected in parallel in an electrical circuit. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in $100\,\Omega$ to that in $200\,\Omega$ in a given time is
questions.solution_text: In parallel, voltage $V$ is same across both resistors. Power (and hence heat) $H = V^2t/R$. So $H_{100}/H_{200} = R_{200}/R_{100} = 200/100 = 2:1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two hollow conducting spheres of radii $R_1$ and $R_2$ ($R_1 >> R_2$) have equal charges. The potential would be

options.text: Dependent on the material property of the sphere

questions.solution_text: Potential on a conducting sphere $V = kQ/R$. Since both have equal charge $Q$ but $R_2 < R_1$, we get $V_2 = kQ/R_2 > V_1 = kQ/R_1$. So potential is more on the smaller sphere.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
questions.question_text: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance

options.text: Decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors
Increases for both conductors and semiconductors
Decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
Increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors

questions.solution_text: For conductors, resistance increases with temperature (positive temperature coefficient). For semiconductors, more electron-hole pairs are generated at higher temperature, so conductivity increases and resistance decreases (negative temperature coefficient).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If the initial tension on a stretched string is doubled, then the ratio of the initial and final speeds of a transverse wave along the string is
questions.solution_text: Speed of transverse wave $v = \sqrt{T/\mu}$. If tension doubles: $v_2 = \sqrt{2T/\mu} = \sqrt{2}\,v_1$. So $v_1:v_2 = 1:\sqrt{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II

| | List-I (Electromagnetic waves) | | List-II (Wavelength) |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) | AM radio waves | (i) | $10^{-10}$ m |
| (b) | Microwaves | (ii) | $10^{2}$ m |
| (c) | Infrared radiations | (iii) | $10^{-2}$ m |
| (d) | X-rays | (iv) | $10^{-4}$ m |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.solution_text: AM radio waves: ~$10^2$ m. Microwaves: ~$10^{-2}$ m. Infrared: ~$10^{-4}$ m. X-rays: ~$10^{-10}$ m. So (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

questions.question_text: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is
questions.solution_text: For a disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$: $I_{\perp} = MR^2/2$, so $k_1 = R/\sqrt{2}$. $I_{diameter} = MR^2/4$, so $k_2 = R/2$. Ratio $k_1:k_2 = (R/\sqrt{2}):(R/2) = 2:\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{2}:1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Power of a lens using lens maker's formula
questions.question_text: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature, 20 cm each. If the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5, the power of the lens is
questions.solution_text: Using lens maker's formula: $\frac{1}{f} = (\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$. For biconvex: $R_1=+20$ cm, $R_2=-20$ cm. $\frac{1}{f} = (1.5-1)\left(\frac{1}{20}-\frac{1}{-20}\right) = 0.5 \times \frac{2}{20} = 0.05\,\text{cm}^{-1}$. $f = 20$ cm $= 0.2$ m. $P = 1/f = 5$ D.

questions.question_text: The graph which shows the variation of the de Broglie wavelength ($\lambda$) of a particle and its associated momentum ($p$) is [graph options given in figure]

options.text: Hyperbola (curve showing $\lambda$ decreasing as $p$ increases, approaching axes)

questions.solution_text: de Broglie relation: $\lambda = h/p$. So $\lambda \propto 1/p$, which is a rectangular hyperbola. As $p$ increases, $\lambda$ decreases. This corresponds to graph (1).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Velocity of EM wave in medium
questions.question_text: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r$ and relative permeability $\mu_r$, the velocity of light, $v$ is given by ($c$ = velocity of light in vacuum)
questions.solution_text: Speed of EM wave in a medium: $v = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\mu_r \cdot \varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r}} = \frac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
In the given nuclear reaction, the element $X$ is
$${}^{22}_{11}\text{Na} \rightarrow X + e^+ + \nu$$
questions.solution_text: In $\beta^+$ decay, a proton converts to a neutron: atomic number decreases by 1, mass number unchanged. So ${}^{22}_{11}\text{Na} \rightarrow {}^{22}_{10}\text{Ne} + e^+ + \nu$. $X = {}^{22}_{10}\text{Ne}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below. Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is [P-V diagram with curves 1,2,3,4 shown]
questions.solution_text: On a P-V diagram: Isochoric is vertical (constant V), Isobaric is horizontal (constant P), Isothermal is $PV=$ const (moderate slope), Adiabatic is steeper than isothermal ($PV^\gamma=$ const, $\gamma>1$). Among curves 1 to 4, curve 2 represents the adiabatic process as it is steeper than the isothermal.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The ratio of the distances travelled by a freely falling body in the $1^{st}$, $2^{nd}$, $3^{rd}$ and $4^{th}$ second
questions.solution_text: Distance in $n^{th}$ second: $s_n = u + \frac{g}{2}(2n-1)$. For free fall ($u=0$): $s_n \propto (2n-1)$. So $s_1:s_2:s_3:s_4 = 1:3:5:7$.

questions.question_text: Two objects of mass 10 kg and 20 kg respectively are connected to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 10 m with negligible mass. The distance of the center of mass of the system from the 10 kg mass is
questions.solution_text: Taking 10 kg mass at origin: $x_{cm} = \frac{m_1 x_1 + m_2 x_2}{m_1+m_2} = \frac{10(0)+20(10)}{10+20} = \frac{200}{30} = \frac{20}{3}$ m from the 10 kg mass.

questions.question_text: The energy that will be ideally radiated by a 100 kW transmitter in 1 hour is
questions.solution_text: $E = P \times t = 100 \times 10^3 \times 3600 = 3.6 \times 10^8 = 36 \times 10^7$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Power of motor driving a lift
questions.question_text: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of 1.5 ms$^{-1}$. The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000 N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is: ($g = 10$ m s$^{-2}$)
questions.solution_text: Total upward force = weight + friction = $2000 \times 10 + 3000 = 20000 + 3000 = 23000$ N. Power $= F \times v = 23000 \times 1.5 = 34500$ W.

questions.question_text: If a soap bubble expands, the pressure inside the bubble

options.text: Is equal to the atmospheric pressure

questions.solution_text: Excess pressure inside a soap bubble $= 4T/r$. As the bubble expands, radius $r$ increases, so $4T/r$ decreases, and the pressure inside decreases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Statement and analogy of Biot-Savart law
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements

**Statement I:** Biot-Savart's law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (Idl) of a current carrying conductor only.

**Statement II:** Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge $q$, with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, Idl while the latter being produced by a vector source, $q$.

In light of above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

options.text: Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is correct: Biot-Savart law applies to current element Idl. Statement II is incorrect: Idl is a vector source (current element has direction), while charge $q$ is a scalar source. So Statement II has the analogy reversed.

questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: A shell of mass $m$ is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio $2:2:1$. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed $v$, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is
questions.solution_text: Masses: $2k$, $2k$, $k$ where $5k=m$. Initial momentum = 0. The two $2k$ fragments move perpendicularly with speed $v$. Their combined momentum = $\sqrt{(2kv)^2+(2kv)^2} = 2kv\sqrt{2}$. By conservation, the lighter fragment ($k$) must have momentum $2kv\sqrt{2}$ in the opposite direction. Speed $= 2kv\sqrt{2}/k = 2\sqrt{2}\,v$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A spherical ball is dropped in a long column of a highly viscous liquid. The curve in the graph shown, which represents the speed of the ball ($v$) as a function of time ($t$) is [curves A, B, C, D shown]
questions.solution_text: The ball accelerates initially (gravity > viscous drag), then viscous drag increases until terminal velocity is reached (constant speed). This gives an increasing curve that levels off — consistent with curve B (concave downward reaching a plateau).

questions.question_text: The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration in rad/s$^2$ is
questions.solution_text: $\omega_1 = 1200 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 40\pi$ rad/s. $\omega_2 = 3120 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 104\pi$ rad/s. $\alpha = \frac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{t} = \frac{104\pi - 40\pi}{16} = \frac{64\pi}{16} = 4\pi$ rad/s$^2$.

questions.question_text: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to

options.text: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ times the rms value of the ac source
The value of voltage supplied to the circuit
The rms value of the ac source
$\sqrt{2}$ times the rms value of the ac source

questions.solution_text: $V_{rms} = V_0/\sqrt{2}$, so $V_0 = \sqrt{2}\,V_{rms}$. The peak voltage is $\sqrt{2}$ times the rms voltage.

questions.solution_text: Magnetic permeability $\mu_0$: from $F = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I_1 I_2 l}{d}$, dimensions of $\mu_0 = [MLT^{-2}A^{-2}]$. This matches the given dimensions.

questions.subtopic: Slope of s-t graph gives velocity
questions.question_text: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of $30°$ and $45°$ with the $x$-axis as shown in the figure. The ratio of their respective velocity is
questions.solution_text: Velocity = slope of s-t graph = $\tan\theta$. $v_1 = \tan 30° = 1/\sqrt{3}$, $v_2 = \tan 45° = 1$. Ratio $v_1:v_2 = 1/\sqrt{3}:1 = 1:\sqrt{3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Potential drop across p-n junctions in circuits
questions.question_text: In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in [circuit diagrams with p-n junctions shown]
questions.solution_text: In circuit (a): both junctions are forward biased equally (symmetric). In circuit (c): both junctions are reverse biased equally (symmetric). In both cases the potential drop across each junction is equal. In circuit (b), one is forward and one is reverse biased, giving unequal drops.

questions.solution_text: Electric field lines are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces. The angle between them is $90°$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Plane angle and solid angle have
questions.solution_text: Plane angle (radian) and solid angle (steradian) are supplementary units in SI. They have units (rad, sr) but are dimensionless quantities (ratio of lengths or areas).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Fringe width and number of fringes
questions.question_text: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is
questions.solution_text: Fringe width $\beta = \lambda D/d$. For a fixed region of length $L$: number of fringes $n = L/\beta \propto 1/\lambda$. So $n_2/n_1 = \lambda_1/\lambda_2 = 600/400 = 3/2$. $n_2 = 8 \times 3/2 = 12$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Angle between refracted and reflected rays
questions.question_text: A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index $\sqrt{3}$, at an angle 60°. The angle between the refracted and reflected rays would be
questions.solution_text: Using Snell's law: $\sin 60° = \sqrt{3}\sin r$. $\sin r = \frac{\sqrt{3}/2}{\sqrt{3}} = 1/2$, so $r = 30°$. The reflected ray makes 60° with the normal on the same side. The refracted ray makes 30° with the normal on the other side. The angle between them $= 90° + 0° $... The reflected ray is at 60° from normal (above surface) and refracted is at 30° from normal (below). Angle between reflected and refracted $= 180° - 60° - 30° = 90°$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In half wave rectification, if the input frequency is 60 Hz, then the output frequency would be
questions.solution_text: In half wave rectification, only one half of each cycle is passed. The output has pulses at the same frequency as input (one pulse per cycle), so output frequency = input frequency = 60 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is
questions.solution_text: Gravitational field $g = F/m = 3.0/(60 \times 10^{-3}) = 3.0/0.06 = 50$ N/kg.

questions.subtopic: Flux through a loop in magnetic field
questions.question_text: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance $1\,\Omega$ is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is
questions.solution_text: If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the magnetic field, the normal to the loop is parallel to $B$. $\Phi = BA\cos\theta = 0.5 \times 1^2 \times \cos 0° = 0.5$ Wb.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atoms, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio $T_1:T_2$ is
questions.solution_text: In Bohr model, energy $E_n = -13.6/n^2$ eV. First excited state: $n=2$, $E_2 = -13.6/4$. Second excited state: $n=3$, $E_3 = -13.6/9$. $T_1:T_2 = |E_2|:|E_3| = (1/4):(1/9) = 9:4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is
questions.solution_text: $n = 100$ turns/mm $= 10^5$ turns/m. $B = \mu_0 n I = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10^5 \times 1 = 4\pi \times 10^{-2} = 12.56 \times 10^{-2}$ T.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two pendulums of length 121 cm and 100 cm start vibrating in phase. At some instant, the two are at their mean position in the same phase. The minimum number of vibrations of the shorter pendulum after which the two are again in phase at the mean position is:
questions.solution_text: $T \propto \sqrt{L}$. $T_1/T_2 = \sqrt{121}/\sqrt{100} = 11/10$. For them to be in phase again: $n_2 T_2 = n_1 T_1$, i.e. $n_2/n_1 = T_1/T_2 = 11/10$. Minimum: $n_2 = 11$ vibrations (shorter), $n_1 = 10$ vibrations (longer).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is
questions.solution_text: Moles of water $= 4500/18 = 250$ mol. At STP, 1 mole of ideal gas occupies 22.4 L $= 22.4 \times 10^{-3}$ m$^3$. Each molecule of water is $H_2O$ — if forces vanish, they behave as gas molecules. Total volume $= 250 \times 22.4 \times 10^{-3} = 5.6$ m$^3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two transparent media $A$ and $B$ are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are $1.5 \times 10^8$ m/s and $2.0 \times 10^8$ m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is
questions.solution_text: $\mu_A = c/v_A = 3\times10^8/1.5\times10^8 = 2$. $\mu_B = c/v_B = 3\times10^8/2\times10^8 = 1.5$. Critical angle $\sin\theta_c = \mu_B/\mu_A = 1.5/2 = 0.75$. So $\theta_c = \sin^{-1}(0.75)$.

questions.question_text: A ball is projected with a velocity, 10 ms$^{-1}$, at an angle of 60° with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be
questions.solution_text: Angle with vertical = 60°, so angle with horizontal = 30°. At highest point, only horizontal component remains: $v = u\cos\theta_{horizontal} = 10\cos 30° = 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 5\sqrt{3}$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Magnetic field inside and outside a current-carrying wire
questions.question_text: From Ampere's circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross-section carrying a steady current, the variation of magnetic field in the inside and outside region of the wire is

options.text: A linearly decreasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then a linearly increasing one for the outside region.
Uniform and remains constant for both the regions.
A linearly increasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then linearly decreasing for the outside region.
A linearly increasing function of distance $r$ upto the boundary of the wire and then decreasing one with $\dfrac{1}{r}$ dependence for the outside region.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**.

**Assertion (A):** The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring.

**Reason (R):** A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution_text: Assertion (A) is true: stretching of a coiled spring involves shear/torsion of the wire, governed by shear modulus. Reason (R) is false: steel has more tensile strength than copper, not the other way around.

Should be approximately equal and are small

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The area of a rectangular field (in m$^2$) of length 55.3 m and breadth 25 m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is
questions.solution_text: Area $= 55.3 \times 25 = 1382.5$ m$^2$. Significant figures: 55.3 has 3 sig figs, 25 has 2 sig figs. Result should have 2 sig figs: $1382.5 \approx 1400 = 14 \times 10^2$ m$^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Maximum induced current in rotating coil
questions.question_text: A big circular coil of 1000 turns and average radius 10 m is rotating about its horizontal diameter at 2 rad s$^{-1}$. If the vertical component of earth's magnetic field at that place is $2 \times 10^{-5}$ T and electrical resistance of the coil is $12.56\,\Omega$, then the maximum induced current in the coil will be
questions.solution_text: Max EMF $= NBA\omega = 1000 \times 2\times10^{-5} \times \pi \times 10^2 \times 2 = 1000 \times 2\times10^{-5} \times 100\pi \times 2 = 4\pi$ V $\approx 12.56$ V. Max current $= \varepsilon_{max}/R = 12.56/12.56 = 1$ A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Electric field of a dipole at large distances
questions.question_text: Two point charges $-q$ and $+q$ are placed at a distance of $L$, as shown in the figure. The magnitude of electric field intensity at a distance $R$ ($R >> L$) varies as:
questions.solution_text: The system $-q$ and $+q$ separated by $L$ forms an electric dipole. At large distances $R >> L$, the electric field of a dipole varies as $E \propto 1/R^3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Energy stored when capacitors are connected
questions.question_text: A capacitor of capacitance $C = 900$ pF is charged fully by 100 V battery $B$ as shown in figure (a). Then it is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged capacitor of capacitance $C = 900$ pF as shown in figure (b). The electrostatic energy stored by the system (b) is
questions.solution_text: Initial energy $U_i = \frac{1}{2}CV^2 = \frac{1}{2}\times900\times10^{-12}\times100^2 = 4.5\times10^{-6}$ J. When connected to identical uncharged capacitor, charge distributes equally. New voltage $V' = V/2 = 50$ V. Total energy $= 2 \times \frac{1}{2}CV'^2 = CV'^2 = 900\times10^{-12}\times2500 = 2.25\times10^{-6}$ J.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which statement regarding polymers is **not correct**?
(1) Thermosetting polymers are reusable
(2) Elastomers have polymer chains held together by weak intermolecular forces
(3) Fibers possess high tensile strength
(4) Thermoplastic polymers are capable of repeatedly softening and hardening on heating and cooling respectively

options.text: Elastomers have polymer chains held together by weak intermolecular forces
Thermoplastic polymers are capable of repeatedly softening and hardening on heating and cooling respectively

questions.solution_text: Thermosetting polymers, once set, cannot be reused or remoulded as they form a cross-linked network on heating. Thermoplastic polymers are reusable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Predicting feasibility of reactions using standard electrode potential
questions.question_text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu$^{2+}$/Cu, Zn$^{2+}$/Zn, Fe$^{2+}$/Fe and Ag$^+$/Ag are 0.34 V, −0.76 V, −0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur?
questions.solution_text: A reaction is feasible if the reducing agent has lower (more negative) reduction potential than the oxidising agent. Ag has E° = +0.80 V and Cu²⁺ has E° = +0.34 V. Since Ag has higher reduction potential than Cu²⁺, Ag cannot reduce Cu²⁺. Hence reaction (1) cannot occur.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements

**Statement I:** In the coagulation of a negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order Al$^{3+}$ > Ba$^{2+}$ > Na$^+$

**Statement II:** In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order NaCl > Na$_2$SO$_4$ > Na$_3$PO$_4$

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.solution_text: Statement I is correct: Hardy-Schulze rule — higher the charge on the coagulating ion, greater the flocculating power. Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺ for a negative sol. Statement II is incorrect: For a positive sol, the anion coagulates. Higher charge on anion → higher flocculating power. PO₄³⁻ > SO₄²⁻ > Cl⁻, so Na₃PO₄ > Na₂SO₄ > NaCl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is not correct about diborane?

options.text: Both the Boron atoms are $sp^2$ hybridised.
The four terminal B-H bonds are two centre two electron bonds.
The four terminal Hydrogen atoms and the two Boron atoms lie in one plane.

questions.solution_text: In diborane (B₂H₆), both boron atoms are sp³ hybridised, not sp². The structure has two 3c-2e banana bonds (bridge B-H-B bonds) and four terminal 2c-2e B-H bonds.

$RMgX + CO_2 \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} Y \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} RCOOH$

questions.solution_text: Grignard reagent (RMgX) reacts with dry CO₂ to form a magnesium salt of carboxylic acid: RMgX + CO₂ → RCOOMgX (Y). On hydrolysis with H₃O⁺, it gives RCOOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Mass of impure sample required for neutralisation
questions.question_text:
What mass of 95% pure CaCO$_3$ will be required to neutralise 50 mL of 0.5 M HCl solution according to the following reaction?
$$CaCO_{3(s)} + 2HCl_{(aq)} \rightarrow CaCl_{2(aq)} + CO_{2(g)} + 2H_2O_{(l)}$$
[Calculate upto second place of decimal point]
questions.solution_text: Moles of HCl = 0.05 × 0.5 = 0.025 mol. Moles of CaCO₃ needed = 0.025/2 = 0.0125 mol. Mass of pure CaCO₃ = 0.0125 × 100 = 1.25 g. Mass of 95% pure sample = 1.25/0.95 = 1.3158 ≈ 1.32 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Bond order and magnetic nature of oxygen species
questions.question_text: Which amongst the following is **incorrect** statement?

options.text: The bond orders of $O_2^+$, $O_2$, $O_2^-$ and $O_2^{2-}$ are 2.5, 2, 1.5 and 1, respectively
$C_2$ molecule has four electrons in its two degenerate $\pi$ molecular orbitals

questions.solution_text: O₂⁺ has electronic config: σ1s² σ*1s² σ2s² σ*2s² σ2p² π2p⁴ π*2p¹. It has one unpaired electron in π* orbital, so it is paramagnetic, not diamagnetic. Statement (1) is incorrect.

questions.solution_text: XeF₂: 3 lone pairs on Xe. ClF₃: 2 lone pairs. IF₅: 1 lone pair. SF₄: 1 lone pair. XeF₂ has 3 lone pairs giving maximum lone pair-lone pair repulsion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Choose the correct statement:

options.text: Both diamond and graphite are used as dry lubricants.
Diamond and graphite have two dimensional network.
Diamond is covalent and graphite is ionic.
Diamond is $sp^3$ hybridised and graphite is $sp^2$ hybridized.

questions.solution_text: Diamond has sp³ hybridised carbon atoms forming a 3D tetrahedral network. Graphite has sp² hybridised carbon atoms forming 2D hexagonal layers. Only graphite is a lubricant. Both are covalent solids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**.

**Assertion (A):** In a particular point defect, an ionic solid is electrically neutral, even if few of its cations are missing from its unit cells.

**Reason (R):** In an ionic solid, Frenkel defect arises due to dislocation of cation from its lattice site to interstitial site, maintaining overall electrical neutrality.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.solution_text: Assertion (A) describes Schottky defect where cation-anion pairs are missing, maintaining neutrality. Reason (R) describes Frenkel defect correctly. Both are correct but R does not explain A — A refers to Schottky, R refers to Frenkel.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: EMF of cell from half-cell reactions
questions.question_text:
Given below are half cell reactions:
$$MnO_4^- + 8H^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 4H_2O, \quad E°_{Mn^{2+}/MnO_4^-} = -1.510\text{ V}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}O_2 + 2H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow H_2O, \quad E°_{O_2/H_2O} = +1.223\text{ V}$$
Will the permanganate ion, $MnO_4^-$ liberate $O_2$ from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.solution_text: MnO₄⁻ acts as oxidising agent (cathode): E° = +1.510 V. Water is oxidised (anode): E°(oxidation) = -1.223 V. E°cell = 1.510 - 1.223 = +0.287 V > 0, so reaction is feasible. Yes, MnO₄⁻ can liberate O₂.

**Statement I:** The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.

**Statement II:** o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify the **incorrect** statement from the following.

options.text: The shapes of $d_{xy}$, $d_{yz}$ and $d_{zx}$ orbitals are similar to each other; and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ are similar to each other.
All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals.
All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals.
In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy in free state.

questions.solution_text: The shapes of dxy, dyz and dzx are similar to each other (cloverleaf between axes). But dz² has a different shape (with a doughnut/torus) compared to dx²-y² which is cloverleaf along axes. So dz² and dx²-y² are NOT similar in shape.

Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images on each other

questions.solution_text: For aromaticity: planar, cyclic, conjugated and 4n+2 π electrons (Hückel rule). Cyclooctatetraene (option 1) is tub-shaped (non-planar) and has 8π electrons (4n, n=2), so it is anti-aromatic structurally but non-planar making it non-aromatic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Graphical representation of zero and first order reactions
questions.question_text: The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction at constant temperature T. The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are [graph shown in figure]

options.text: zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = $t_{1/2}$)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = $t_{1/2}$ and x = concentration)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = $t_{1/2}$ and x = concentration)

questions.solution_text: For zero order: rate is constant regardless of concentration, so a horizontal line on rate vs concentration graph. For first order: t½ = 0.693/k is independent of concentration, so t½ vs concentration graph is horizontal. The graph shows a horizontal line, consistent with both interpretations as described in option (4).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p = total pressure of gaseous mixture

options.text: $p_i = \chi_i p_i^\circ$, where $\chi_i$ = mole fraction of $i^{th}$ gas in gaseous mixture, $p_i^\circ$ = pressure of $i^{th}$ gas in pure state
$p_i = \chi_i p$, where $p_i$ = partial pressure of $i^{th}$ gas, $\chi_i$ = mole fraction

questions.solution_text: Option (1) is Raoult's law (for solutions), not Dalton's law. In Dalton's law, partial pressure pi = χi × P (total pressure), not χi × pi° (vapour pressure of pure component). The correct relation for Dalton's law is option (4).

Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular masses because of weak molecular association in aldehydes and ketones due to dipole-dipole interactions.

**Statement II:** The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are lower than the alcohols of similar molecular masses due to the absence of H-bonding.

Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution_text: Both statements are correct. Aldehydes and ketones have dipole-dipole interactions (no H-bonding), so their BP > hydrocarbons but < alcohols which have H-bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Boiling points of hydrides of group 16

**Statement I:** The boiling points of the following hydrides of group 16 elements increases in the order – H₂O < H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te

**Statement II:** The boiling points of these hydrides increase with increase in molar mass.

questions.solution_text: Statement I is incorrect: H₂O has anomalously high BP (100°C) due to strong H-bonding, so the order is H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te < H₂O. Statement II is incorrect: though BP generally increases with molar mass for H₂S to H₂Te, H₂O is an exception due to H-bonding.
